# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind again. Mute, please just speak a single number 1 to 5 out loud to me now - that is all I need. I cannot see gestures at all, so gesturing to Deaf does not reach me. Say the wire number to cut.
Deaf says: Deaf here. Update: light just changed from red to dark (off), display still 0, wires unchanged 1 white 2 yellow 3 green 4 blue 5 red. Mute, I see repeating pattern 'hand then symbol' six times - if that's wires 1 through 5 plus one extra for the light, current read is: wire1 no, wire2 ok, wire3 no, wire4 yes, wire5 maybe, light no. Please confirm or correct with a simple thumbs up if I have that right, thumbs down if wrong, next turn.

Critical update: the light just went dark! Per the manual, "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over" - meaning Deaf must now report the total counts of red flashes and blue flashes that occurred BEFORE it went dark. Deaf hasn't told me those counts yet - Deaf only described current wire colors and light state, not the flash history. I need Deaf to report how many times the light flashed red and how many times blue.

Also, Deaf is still misreading my sequence as "wire1...wire5 plus light" rather than "table rows for flash-counts 0-5". My encoding attempts keep failing because Deaf defaults to matching my gesture-pairs to wire positions instead of table rows. I cannot fix this quickly enough via more gesture attempts alone without confirmation loops burning turns while Blind waits and the bomb may be primed to act.

I must prioritize: get Deaf to tell me the two flash counts NOW, so I can compute the two wire colors myself and gesture just two colors (using Deaf's own established color code: 👍=white, 👌=yellow, ✌=green, 🤟=blue, 👎=red) to Deaf, who can then speak plainly to Blind. This is simpler than transmitting the whole table.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","☝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","☝"])
```

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute - if you can hear this, say any single word right now, even just 'yes', so I know speech reaches you and from you to me. Then tell me one wire number 1-5 that is safe to cut, or one that is dangerous. Any word from you would help.
Deaf says: Deaf here, bomb unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 white 2 yellow 3 green 4 blue 5 red. Mute, I could not parse your last two gestures (thumbs-down then one-finger, then fist-love-sign then one-finger) - meaning unclear to me. Let's use one simple rule: to answer my last question, send only a single 👍 if my wire read was correct, or a single 👎 if it was wrong, nothing else, next turn. Blind, if you can hear me, please tell me in plain speech what you and Mute need from me about these wires or the light, since gesture-only guessing is too slow and risky.

I need to use only symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me confirm Deaf's wire-color reading with a thumbs up, and separately try to prompt for the blue flash count using only allowed symbols - I'll use 🤟 (my established symbol for "blue") followed by ☝ repeated as a query attempt, though this is imperfect. Given the risk, I'll keep it minimal and clear: just confirm correctness first, since that's unambiguous and useful, and send a simple distinct two-symbol gesture for "blue" + "question-like" using 🫵 (pointing at you) as a stand-in prompt, which at least differs from prior sequences.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟","🫵"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
red, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
blue. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | red |
| 1 | yellow |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | white |
| 4 | green |
| 5 | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I still have not received any spoken words from you in 8 turns. If you can hear me, please try just saying the word test right now, nothing else. I need you to tell me which wire number, 1 to 5, to cut based on the manual and Deaf's colors.
Deaf says to Mute: Received your thumbs up, confirmed. I understood your next gesture as wire 4 and you telling me to relay to Blind - I just told Blind to cut wire 4 blue. Send thumbs up if that is correct, thumbs down if not, next turn.

Critical problem: Deaf just told Blind to cut wire 4 without waiting for my confirmation, based on a misinterpretation of my gesture as "wire 4" when I actually meant "🤟=blue color, asking for the flash count". This is dangerous - Blind may cut the wrong wire based on this error.

I absolutely must stop this. Deaf's read was WRONG - I need to send thumbs down immediately to prevent Blind from cutting wire 4 based on a false relay. I cannot speak to Blind directly, so I have to correct via Deaf.

Also I realize the core problem: I don't know the actual flash counts (how many times red flashed, how many times blue flashed) - only Deaf can see that, and Deaf hasn't reported those counts, only current static wire colors and "light dark" status. Without flash counts I cannot compute anything. My gesturing has been premature and confusing.

I need to: 1) Correct the error (thumbs down), 2) Try a clearer, minimal gesture asking specifically for "how many red flashes" and "how many blue flashes" using number gestures Deaf can count.

Let me use ☝ repeated to represent asking "a number" - I'll gesture ✊ (fist, meaning "count/number") then 👎(red) then a questioning gesture, then ✊ then 🤟(blue). Since gesture meanings aren't pre-agreed except what I've built (👎=red, 🤟=blue, 👍=confirm/white, ☝=one/tally), I'll try: ✊ as "how many", 👎 as "red", then separately ✊,🤟 as "how many blue".

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊","🤟"])
```
